memory_update.text: Core public-market candidates for housing repair/remodel substitution node: HD, LOW, FERG, WSO, INVH.
Best direct mappings are Pro-focused home improvement retail, plumbing/HVAC distribution, HVAC replacement distribution, and institutional single-family rental maintenance demand.

Not yet covered in this five-name pass: paint/flooring specialists such as SHW and FND, appliance makers such as WHR, home-services platforms such as ANGI, storage/moving names, and smaller repair-service consolidators.
Need a later pass to separate necessary repair/maintenance exposure from discretionary remodel/furnishings exposure and to quantify Pro versus DIY mix by company.

WSO should be tracked as the cleanest HVAC/R distributor candidate for the housing repair/replacement chokepoint, especially around residential replacement units, parts/supplies, refrigerant transition, and contractor channel capacity.
FERG broadens node coverage beyond HVAC into plumbing, waterworks, appliances, PVF, and pro-channel repair/maintenance distribution; less pure but important for scarce fulfillment capacity.
AOS is a direct necessary-replacement equipment exposure: water heaters and boilers are less discretionary than furniture/flooring and may be more tied to installed-base age than housing turnover.

BLD adds an installer-capacity and specialty-distribution angle for insulation, roofing, and energy-efficiency retrofits; relevance depends on mix shift away from new construction toward repair/remodel and maintenance.

Next pass should test additional public exposures in electrical distribution, roofing materials, paint/coatings, rental-home maintenance operators, home-services software, and contractor roll-up platforms; this pass intentionally prioritized scarce suppliers/equipment/distribution rather than downstream retailers.

WSO, FERG and CSW form a professional-channel repair/remodel supplier cluster across HVAC/R, plumbing and electrical that may be more directly tied to necessary home maintenance than discretionary furnishings.

FTDR is an adjacent home-services platform candidate; inclusion depends on whether recurring warranty renewals and service-call economics can offset claims inflation, contractor-quality risk and weak real-estate transaction channels.
INVH should be tracked as a scaled demand aggregator/customer for single-family rental repairs, turnover work and home-system maintenance rather than as a supplier.

Obvious retailers HD and LOW, appliance/furnishing names, paint/flooring names, and moving/storage companies were not included due to the five-candidate limit and this pass's focus on less obvious second-order beneficiaries.
Need a separate pass for manufacturers upstream of repair channels: HVAC OEMs, water-heater makers, plumbing fixtures, electrical products, roofing, paint, flooring and building-envelope suppliers.

node: Housing-linked consumer spend: home improvement, repair, maintenance, furnishings, rentership, and home services
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct public-company universe for the housing repair/remodel substitution node. The strongest direct exposures are large home-improvement retailers with Pro and repair/remodel demand, specialized plumbing/HVAC distributors tied to replacement and contractor capacity, and scaled single-family rental asset owners whose maintenance capex creates recurring downstream demand. This is a research universe only, not a buy/sell list. For this node, the most relevant scarce or capacity-constrained public-market exposures are not discretionary furniture retailers, but HVAC/R distribution, plumbing/HVAC/waterworks distribution, replacement equipment OEMs, water-heater/boiler manufacturers, and insulation/roofing/building-products installers-distributors. These companies sit closer to non-deferrable repair, replacement, contractor capacity, code/regulatory transitions, parts availability, and pro-channel fulfillment than to housing transaction volume alone. Expanded universe for the repair/remodel substitution node emphasizes second-order exposure rather than discretionary furnishings. The strongest mappings are professional-channel distributors and contractor-facing suppliers tied to HVAC, plumbing, electrical, water systems, home warranties, and single-family rental maintenance. Initial evidence supports the idea that weak housing turnover and soft big-ticket replacement can still leave pockets of recurring, necessary repair demand, but several candidates need further proof that repair mix offsets housing-cycle weakness.
